context: 3 Discussion We conjecture (but could not prove) that our lower bound examples (cf. [4]) are really worst-case examples, and that the values of our linear programs converge to these bounds. Another question is whether the master route ratio is 1−e1−1/2 even for low-activity instances. Currently we only know the upper bound of 3 from [25], but know no example with master route ratio larger than 1−e1−1/2 (and this value is attained by our example only as the activity tends to infinity). The analogous question applies to the sampling algorithm: whether we need to consider the low-activity case separately is an open question. Finally, we hope that our approach can also help for proving a better bound for related problems where similar random sampling techniques are used, or for showing that known bounds are best possible.
